rationale: In the old implementation, BishopPairValue was evaluated symmetrically with pawn count damping such that it had zero derivative in positions with equal pawn counts or saturated thresholds. The value of having two bishops vs bishop+knight or two knights is one of the most fundamental classical positional advantages in chess. Restoring BishopPairValue as a clean non-saturating bonus makes it identifiable and tunable.

When 30 raw Endgame attack parameters were collapsed, their values were tied to the MiddleGame threat tiers via an empirical 1.4x factor. The relative escalation of tactical threats as pieces come off the board (threat of mate, skewer, or pawn win increases in value relative to remaining material) is an independent chess concept that should be tunable rather than a hardcoded magic number.

EdgeWeight and CornerWeight exhibited r = -0.985 collinearity. The 72/22 ratio guarantees strict mathematical monotonicity toward the corner across all 64 squares for bare-king mates (KQvK, KRvK). Un-tying this would reintroduce the severe collinearity (condition number 27.57) and risk anti-monotonic mate bugs.
A constant evaluation offset in bare king endings that shifts absolute evaluation without altering move ordering, minimax choices, or king drive gradients. Fully absorbed by piece value baselines.

Move counts 9..12 and 13..15 in MG are structurally contiguous saturation steps that had identical values (4 cp). In quiet play, queens rarely reach 15 legal moves without tactical complications. Tying them into a single saturation parameter eliminated redundancy without losing chess expression.
In endgames, extreme queen mobility (>12 moves) is virtually unconstrained. Fixing the terminal increment preserves monotonic saturation while leaving the early and mid activity slope fully tunable.
Pawn attacks near the king are handled by pawn storms and direct contact checks in search/tactics; the parameter was dead and unbacked in production.
